ground_truth.description: MarkdownText calls `uM_T(() => {...}, [text])` as a React hook, but `uM_T` is a non-standard identifier. Unless it is an established alias for `React.useMemo` defined elsewhere (data.js or top of this module), this throws a ReferenceError and crashes the entire Tasks tab whenever a task is selected. The unusual `_T` suffix makes this a strong candidate for a typo of the intended memo alias — the kind of runtime break that passes a static review but fails at render time.

DOMPurify.addHook('afterSanitizeAttributes', ...) registers a process-global hook that forces target=_blank and rel=noopener on EVERY anchor produced by ANY DOMPurify.sanitize call anywhere in the app, not just markdown rendered in the Task Detail pane. Any other current or future consumer of DOMPurify inherits this link behavior unexpectedly.

The useMemo dependency array is only [text]. If `marked`/`DOMPurify` load asynchronously or fail their integrity check on first render, the memo caches `null` and degrades to plain text; once the libraries later become available the memo will not recompute (text unchanged), leaving the description permanently un-rendered as markdown. Library availability is not part of the memo key.

The integrity attributes on the new marked@12.0.0 and dompurify@3.2.4 script tags do not match the bytes unpkg serves (correct values are sha384-NNQgBjjuhtXzPmmy4gurS5X7P4uTt1DThyevz4Ua0IVK5+kazYQI1W27JHjbbxQz and sha384-eEu5CTj3qGvu9PdJuS+YlkNi7d2XxQROAFYOr59zgObtlcux1ae1Il3u7jvdCSWu). Browsers block both scripts, so `marked` and `DOMPurify` are never defined, MarkdownText always takes its plain-text fallback, and the feature never renders markdown; the silent fallback hides the failure.

The old `.desc` rule used `white-space: pre-line`, which preserved single newlines; the change removes it and calls `marked.parse(text)` with default options (`breaks: false`), so line-separated plain-text descriptions/details without blank lines are merged into one run-on paragraph in the rendered path.

A whitespace-only description is truthy, so MarkdownText skips the `empty` ('—') placeholder; marked renders it to an empty string and the Description section shows a blank div. This is not a regression: the old `task.description || '—'` also rendered whitespace-only text as blank.

When `marked` or `DOMPurify` is undefined, MarkdownText silently renders plain text with no console warning or other signal, so a failed CDN load (including an SRI mismatch) is indistinguishable from the pre-change UI.

MarkdownText and the DOMPurify hook carry reviewer-facing rationale comments (why memoise, 'streaming status updates from another tab', the list of CDN failure modes) that justify decisions rather than clarify code; this prose belongs in the commit message and is prone to drift.

No automated check covers the change: nothing asserts index.html carries the marked/DOMPurify script tags with integrity attributes (let alone that the hashes match the pinned files), and no test exercises sanitisation or MarkdownText's branches. The task did not request tests and the dashboard has no JS harness.

task.title: Render Task Detail pane description + details as markdown
task.description: The dashboard Tasks view Task Detail pane currently renders the `description` and `details` fields as raw text. Both fields commonly contain markdown (headings, lists, bold, code spans, fenced code blocks). Render them as formatted HTML using `marked` + `DOMPurify` from the unpkg CDN (same pattern as the existing React/Babel script tags). Apply the same treatment to both fields so they look consistent.
task.details:
**Approach** 1. Add two script tags to `dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/index.html` (next to the existing React/Babel CDN scripts), pinned to specific versions with SRI hashes for consistency with siblings: - `marked` (https://unpkg.com/marked@... — small, mature, fast) - `DOMPurify` (https://unpkg.com/dompurify@...) 2. Bump the `?v=N` cache-buster on the JSX/CSS includes — production users hit Firefox cache hard (see memory `feedback_browser_cache_firefox`). 3. Add a small `MarkdownText` component.
